entities.title: Prachanda loses confidence vote in the House of Representatives

properties.summary: Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda' lost a vote of confidence after CPN-UML withdrew its support. Reporting gives 63 of 275 members in favour, 194 against and one abstention. Oli, with Nepali Congress support, was set to be nominated as the next prime minister.

evidence.note: Business Today dated 12 Jul 2024 reports the vote; ETV Bharat of 15 Jul confirms Prachanda lost the vote of confidence.
The 63/194/1 count and the UML withdrawal are given only by Business Today among retrieved sources.

entities.title: President Paudel appoints Oli as prime minister

properties.summary: President Ram Chandra Paudel appointed CPN-UML chairman KP Sharma Oli as prime minister, after Oli staked his claim with the backing of Nepali Congress president Sher Bahadur Deuba.

evidence.note: All India Radio dated 14 Jul 2024. ETV Bharat (15 Jul) reports the swearing-in on the Monday but not the appointment date.

entities.title: Oli sworn in for a fourth time and forms a 22-member cabinet

properties.summary: KP Sharma Oli was sworn in as prime minister for the fourth time and formed a 22-member cabinet with two deputy prime ministers (Prakash Man Singh of Nepali Congress and Bishnu Prasad Paudel of CPN-UML). President Paudel administered the oath to 19 newly appointed ministers.

evidence.note: Four outlets agree on the date, the 22-member cabinet and the two deputy prime ministers.

Himalayan Times says the oath was administered at 'the Office of the President'; the mapping of that office to the Shital Niwas location record is an inference from the site, not stated in the source.

entities.title: Oli wins a vote of confidence with 188 votes

properties.summary: Oli won the vote of confidence required within 30 days of appointment: 188 of 263 lawmakers present voted in favour, 74 against, one abstained. Oli read out the seven-point Nepali Congress-CPN-UML agreement, which provides for Oli to lead for two years and Sher Bahadur Deuba to lead until the December 2027 general elections.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post and Himal Press give the same count; Himal Press (second article) gives the pact text.

entities.title: Cabinet decides to lift the TikTok ban

properties.summary: At its regular Thursday cabinet meeting the government decided to lift the ban on TikTok that the Dahal government had imposed in November 2023. Communications Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung announced the decision.

evidence.note: Al Jazeera and the wire copy agree on the Thursday cabinet decision; Kantipur dated 21 Aug reports the process under way.

entities.title: NTA orders internet providers to lift the TikTok block

properties.summary: The Nepal Telecommunications Authority ordered internet and mobile service providers to remove the restriction on TikTok, formally ending the ban after the 22 Aug cabinet decision.

evidence.note: Times of Oman (ANI copy) published 7 Sep; the 6 Sep date for the NTA announcement comes from that page's text as retrieved, not from a verbatim sentence.

entities.title: Nationwide floods and landslides, 26-28 September 2024

properties.summary: Heavy late-monsoon rain from 26 to 28 September caused floods and landslides across Nepal, with the worst damage in the Kathmandu Valley. Death tolls differ by source and date (217, 219, 224, 249). The Oli government was criticised for a slow response and weak preparedness.

evidence.note: Dates of the rain are given by Nepal Economic Forum (26 to 28 Sep) and Global Voices (rain began 26 Sep).

224 is the AP figure of 1 Oct 2024 (KSAT, Peninsula Qatar); the KSAT URL still carries the earlier figure 217; Global Voices (2 Oct) gives at least 219; Nepal Economic Forum (May 2025) gives 249. The retrieved sources do not state whether the tolls count the same categories.

entities.title: Cooperative victims end a 108-day protest after an eight-point agreement

properties.summary: Victims of fraudulent savings cooperatives ended a 108-day protest in Kathmandu after reaching an eight-point agreement with the government, according to a 2025 Kathmandu Post editorial.

evidence.note: The editorial dates this as 'March last year' in an editorial published 17 Apr 2025, so March 2024. Month only.

entities.title: Cooperative victims hold a relay hunger strike in Kathmandu and Chitwan

properties.summary: Victims of cooperative fraud protested in Kathmandu and Chitwan over deposits not returned, with a relay hunger strike, and said the protest would continue until an earlier agreement was implemented.

evidence.note: Date is the publication date of the Kantipur report (Jestha 12, 2081 BS); the start of the hunger strike is not stated in the retrieved text.

entities.title: Cooperative victims resume protests (third phase)

properties.summary: After the March agreement, cooperative victims resumed a third phase of protests in June, on the Maitighar-Baneshwar stretch where they had held earlier sit-ins.

evidence.note: The editorial says 'resumed the third phase of protests in June' without a year; read as June 2024 because it follows the March 2024 agreement in the same sentence. Month only.

entities.title: Cooperative victims protest at Maitighar

properties.summary: Cooperative victims staged a protest at Maitighar, Kathmandu, demanding the return of their savings, which they say were embezzled.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post photo story dated 20 Nov 2024; the caption says 'on Wednesday'.

entities.title: Parliamentary committee report finds Lamichhane complicit in cooperative fund misuse

properties.summary: A parliamentary special committee concluded that evidence did not show Rabi Lamichhane to be innocent: funds from cooperatives were funnelled into Gorkha Media Network, where he had been managing director, using cheques he signed.

evidence.note: Republica and the Kathmandu Post (19 Oct) describe the committee findings.
Date is the publication date of the Republica article; the date the report was tabled is not stated in the retrieved text.

entities.title: Rabi Lamichhane arrested on cooperative fraud and organised crime charges

properties.summary: A Central Investigation Bureau team arrested Rabi Lamichhane, a former deputy prime minister, from the Rastriya Swatantra Party's central office in Banasthali, Kathmandu, on charges of cooperative fraud and organised crime. He was taken to Pokhara.

evidence.note: Three outlets agree on date, place, agency and charges.
France 24 describes him as a former deputy premier.

entities.title: Lamichhane supporters protest in Kathmandu and Pokhara; police use tear gas

properties.summary: Police fired tear gas and used water cannon on thousands of supporters of Rabi Lamichhane near the district court. Protesters chanted against Prime Minister Oli and said the charges were politically motivated.

evidence.note: Single report (France 24, dated 20 Oct 2024, 'Sunday'). The article gives no injury or arrest figures.

entities.title: Social Media Bill introduced in the National Assembly

properties.summary: The government introduced the Bill on the Operation, Use and Regulation of Social Media in the National Assembly. Reporting disagrees on the day: Monday 27 Jan (Himalayan Times, 'on Monday'), 29 Jan (Nepal Economic Forum), 9 Feb (CPJ and Kantipur).

evidence.note: See claims for each date. Himalayan Times is dated 30 Jan and says 'on Monday' (27 Jan, derived); Nepal Economic Forum says 29 Jan; CPJ of 14 Feb says 9 Feb; Kantipur headline dated 9 Feb says the bill 'was submitted'. The 29 Jan value is shown here as the middle value only.

entities.title: Journalists' groups and press-freedom bodies criticise the Social Media Bill

properties.summary: The Federation of Nepali Journalists, other journalists' bodies and legal experts criticised the bill as a threat to freedom of expression; on 14 Feb the Committee to Protect Journalists urged lawmakers to reject it. The bill provides fines, licence revocation and prison terms of up to five years for users, and bars anonymous profiles.

evidence.note: Four reports over 30 Jan to 14 Feb 2025.

entities.title: Former king Gyanendra Shah appeals for public support on Democracy Day eve

properties.summary: In a message ahead of Democracy Day, former king Gyanendra Shah called on 'all countrymen' to support him 'for the prosperity and progress of the country'.

evidence.note: Republica, dated 19 Feb 2025. The quoted appeal is as printed; the paper's framing as 'seeks public support' is its own.

entities.title: Pro-monarchy supporters rally at Tribhuvan Airport as Gyanendra returns

properties.summary: Thousands of supporters, Al Jazeera estimating 10,000, gathered at the airport entrance as former king Gyanendra Shah arrived from western Nepal; the Rastriya Prajatantra Party and pro-monarchy groups took part. Riot police blocked demonstrators from the airport premises and passengers had to walk to the terminals.

evidence.note: Both give the date and a crowd in the thousands; only Al Jazeera gives a figure (10,000).

entities.title: Cabinet removes Kulman Ghising as head of the Nepal Electricity Authority

properties.summary: The Cabinet removed Nepal Electricity Authority executive director Kulman Ghising after a standoff over recovering dues from industrialists and over a bilateral energy trade deal with India that he signed on 12 February.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post, 24 Mar 2025, updated 25 Mar.

entities.title: Pro-monarchy protest turns violent at Tinkune; two killed

properties.summary: A pro-monarchy demonstration at Tinkune, Kathmandu, led by businessman Durga Prasai and drawing 'hardly 5,000' people according to the Kathmandu Post, turned violent. Protesters threw stones, set fire to buildings and vehicles; police used tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets. Two people died and 45 were reported injured by the Kathmandu Post; other outlets give different injury figures. Curfew and an army deployment followed.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post, Himalayan Times and Tribune India agree on date, the violence and the curfew.
Both Kathmandu Post articles give two deaths (Suresh Rajak and Sabin Maharjan); other retrieved sources do not contradict it.
Kathmandu Post of 28 Mar says 45; IANS of 8 Apr says hundreds. See claims.

entities.title: Protesters attack media offices at Tinkune; Annapurna Post office set on fire

properties.summary: Protesters set fire to the Annapurna Post office and pelted the Kantipur Television building with stones. Video journalist Suresh Rajak, filming for Avenues Television from the roof of the Annapurna Media Network building, was killed in the fire.

evidence.note: Himalayan Times (28 Mar) and Kathmandu Post (29 Mar) agree on the attacks.
Rajak's death is reported by the Kathmandu Post of 29 Mar among retrieved sources.

entities.title: Curfew imposed in Tinkune, Baneshwar and Koteshwor

properties.summary: The district administration imposed a curfew from 4:25 pm in the Tinkune, Koteshwor, Sinamangal and Baneshwar area. The Kathmandu Post gives 4:25 pm to 10 pm on Friday, later extended until 7 am on Saturday.

evidence.note: Start time 4:25 pm is given by the Kathmandu Post and the Himalayan Times; Tribune India gives the areas without a time.

entities.title: RPP demonstration for the monarchy and the release of arrested leaders (planned)

properties.summary: The Rastriya Prajatantra Party planned a demonstration demanding reinstatement of the monarchy and release of party leaders in custody, with over 2,000 police to be deployed.

evidence.note: IANS dated 8 Apr 2025 describes it as upcoming; whether it went ahead as described is not checked in the retrieved text.

entities.title: Durga Prasai arrested in Bhadrapur, Jhapa, over the Tinkune violence

properties.summary: Police arrested Durga Prasai in Bhadrapur, Jhapa, and brought him to Kathmandu on charges of crimes against the state and organised crime. The Kathmandu District Court remanded him and an associate to 12 days in custody the same day. The two outlets name the associate differently.

evidence.note: Both dated 11 Apr 2025. The arrest hour and exact day of arrest are not stated; 11 Apr is the date of reporting and of the remand.
All India Radio says Dipak Khadka; Himalayan Times says Deepak Bohara (and, in the retrieved page, also 'Deepak Khadka').

entities.title: Court orders pretrial detention of Rabi Lamichhane; he is taken into custody

properties.summary: A court ordered pretrial detention of Rabi Lamichhane in the cooperative fraud case and he was taken into custody from his home.

evidence.note: Himal Press timeline of 5 Apr 2025.

entities.title: Education Minister Bidya Bhattarai resigns

properties.summary: Education Minister Bidya Bhattarai resigned on a Monday. The Kathmandu Post reports differences with Prime Minister Oli and Finance Minister Paudel, over teachers' demands, as the reason; the stated reason was health.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post of Tue 22 Apr says 'on Monday', i.e. 21 Apr (derived). Reasons conflict: health (stated) versus differences with the PM and finance minister (reported).

entities.title: Supreme Court opens suo moto contempt case against the sidhakura.com website

properties.summary: The Supreme Court began a suo moto contempt case against the publisher and editor of the website sidhakura.com for content defaming a justice. This case produced the later extended full bench verdict on registration of online and social media platforms.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post of 17 Aug 2025 says 'On April 28 last year'. Asia News Network copy is the same origin.

entities.title: Supreme Court extended bench rules that online and social media platforms must register

properties.summary: An extended full bench of the Supreme Court, convicting the sidhakura.com publisher and editor of contempt, ruled that domestic or foreign online and social media platforms should be mandatorily registered with the competent authority before operation and that mechanisms should monitor undesirable content.

evidence.note: Asia News Network reprints the Kathmandu Post; one origin.

Kathmandu Post (17 Aug 2025) places the verdict on 29 September 'last year' (2024), as retrieved. CPJ's 4 Sep 2025 piece refers to an '17 August Supreme Court ruling' (as retrieved, not verbatim): it may be using the publication date of the full text.

entities.title: Kathmandu Post reports full text of the Supreme Court registration verdict

properties.summary: The Kathmandu Post reported the full text of the Supreme Court verdict requiring registration of online and social media platforms, eleven days before the ministry's seven-day registration notice.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post, 17 Aug 2025; Asia News Network repeats it on 18 Aug.

entities.title: 'Nepo kid' trend spreads on Nepali social media

properties.summary: Nepali users began exposing the lifestyles of politicians' children and accusing them of misusing public funds, in a trend that came from Indonesia and the Philippines. Sources disagree on whether it began before or after the ban announcement of 28 August.

evidence.note: Daily Star (via ANN, 10 Sep) says the ban came just as the movement was gaining traction; Global Voices (9 Sep) says it emerged following the ban announcement. Start date is month precision only.

entities.title: Dahal government bans TikTok (November 2023)

properties.description: The government of Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal banned TikTok in November 2023, saying it disrupted social harmony, goodwill and spread indecent material. The ban was lifted in August and September 2024.

evidence.note: Both 2024 articles say the previous government banned the app 'in November' / 'last November', i.e. November 2023. The day is not stated.

entities.title: President Paudel appoints Oli prime minister

properties.description: President Ram Chandra Paudel appointed CPN-UML chairman KP Sharma Oli prime minister on the strength of Nepali Congress backing.

document_url.label: K P Sharma Oli appointed Nepal's new Prime Minister

evidence.note: All India Radio, 14 Jul 2024.

entities.title: Oli cabinet of 22 sworn in

properties.description: President Paudel administered the oath of office and secrecy to 19 newly appointed ministers; with the prime minister and two deputy prime ministers the cabinet had 22 members. Portfolios include Home (Ramesh Lekhak, Congress), Foreign Affairs (Arzu Rana, Congress), Finance (Deputy PM Bishnu Prasad Paudel, UML), Defence (Manbir Rai) and Communications (Prithvi Subba Gurung, UML).

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post lists the portfolios; Onlinekhabar and Himalayan Times confirm the 22-member cabinet and the oath.

entities.title: Oli reads out the seven-point Nepali Congress-CPN-UML agreement

properties.description: Oli disclosed the seven-point agreement: a national consensus government, Oli leading for two years from formation, then Nepali Congress president Sher Bahadur Deuba leading until the general elections in December 2027, with commitments on constitutional amendment, the economy and corruption.

document_url.label: Oli discloses contents of seven-point pact reached between NC, UML

evidence.note: Himal Press (text of the pact) and Kathmandu Post (Oli 'read out' the agreement). The date the pact was signed is not stated in retrieved text.

entities.title: Cabinet lifts the TikTok ban

properties.description: At a regular Thursday meeting the cabinet decided to lift the ban on TikTok after Prime Minister Oli directed that all social networking sites be treated equally. The decision followed TikTok's assurances to the government.

document_url.label: Nepal lifts TikTok ban after blocking app over 'social harmony' concerns

evidence.note: Al Jazeera attributes the 'equal treatment' directive to Oli.

entities.title: NTA directs internet providers to lift the TikTok block

properties.description: The Nepal Telecommunications Authority directed all internet and mobile service providers to remove the restriction on TikTok.

document_url.label: Nepal formally ends ban on TikTok, ISPs ordered to lift embargo

evidence.note: Times of Oman (ANI), 7 Sep 2024.

entities.title: Parliamentary special committee report on cooperative fraud names Lamichhane

properties.description: A parliamentary special inquiry committee concluded that Rabi Lamichhane was involved in misusing cooperative funds that were funnelled into Gorkha Media Network.

document_url.label: Cooperative fraud case: Rabi Lamichhane found complicit, Dhanraj Gurung to be investigated

evidence.note: Date is the Republica publication date; tabling date not stated.

entities.title: CIB arrests Rabi Lamichhane

properties.description: A Central Investigation Bureau team arrested Rabi Lamichhane at his party's central office to investigate cooperative fraud and organised crime.

document_url.label: Lamichhane arrested on fraud, organised crime charges

evidence.note: Three outlets agree.

entities.title: Supreme Court verdict: online and social media platforms must register

properties.description: Extended full bench verdict in the contempt case against sidhakura.com stating that domestic or foreign online and social media platforms should be mandatorily registered with the competent authority before operation. Date disputed between sources.

document_url.label: Top court says all social media, online sites must register

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post and its Asia News Network copy (one origin).
29 Sep 2024 (Kathmandu Post) versus an '17 August' ruling (CPJ, as retrieved).

entities.title: Social Media Bill tabled in the National Assembly

properties.description: The Bill on the Operation, Use and Regulation of Social Media was tabled in the National Assembly by Communications Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung. It provides fines up to NPR 2.5 million for operating without registration, prison terms up to five years for users, and bars anonymous accounts. Date disputed (27 Jan, 29 Jan, 9 Feb).

document_url.label: Key highlights and implications of the Social Media Bill 2081 BS (2025 AD)

evidence.note: Nepal Economic Forum and CPJ describe the provisions.
See event of the same date and the three date claims.

entities.title: Cabinet removes Kulman Ghising from the Nepal Electricity Authority

properties.description: The Cabinet decided to remove Nepal Electricity Authority executive director Kulman Ghising and appoint Shakya (as printed) in his place, after a standoff over dues owed by industrialists and an unauthorised energy trade deal with India.

document_url.label: After long standoff, government sacks Kulman Ghising

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post, 24 Mar 2025.

entities.title: Curfew order for Tinkune, Baneshwar and Koteshwor

properties.description: The district administration imposed a curfew from 4:25 pm in Tinkune, Koteshwor and Sinamangal; the Kathmandu Post gives 4:25 pm to 10 pm on Friday, extended until 7 am Saturday.

document_url.label: Protest leaders incite violence which turns deadly

evidence.note: The issuing office is named only as 'the District Administration' in the Kathmandu Post.

entities.title: Nepal Army deployed in Koteshwor after the curfew

properties.description: The Nepal Army was deployed on the streets of Koteshwor to restore order after the curfew began.

document_url.label: Pro-monarchy protesters attack media offices, set fire to Annapurna Post office

evidence.note: Himalayan Times, 28 Mar 2025.

entities.title: Minister Gurung vows accountability for the Tinkune violence

properties.description: Communications Minister and government spokesperson Prithvi Subba Gurung said the guilty would be held accountable, and condemned attacks on media houses; the report mentions a probe committee.

document_url.label: Nepal government spokesperson minister Gurung vows legal action against guilty of Friday's violent protests

evidence.note: All India Radio paraphrases; no verbatim sentence from the minister was retrieved.

entities.title: Police arrest Durga Prasai

properties.description: Nepal Police arrested Durga Prasai and an associate in Bhadrapur, Jhapa, on charges of crimes against the state and organised crime linked to the 28 March violence.

document_url.label: Nepal police arrest medical entrepreneur, political activist Durga Prasai

evidence.note: Date is the reporting date; arrest day not stated.

entities.title: Kathmandu District Court remands Durga Prasai for 12 days

properties.description: The Kathmandu District Court remanded Durga Prasai and an associate to judicial custody for 12 days for further investigation.

document_url.label: Durga Prasai sent to judicial custody for 12 days

evidence.note: Himalayan Times, 11 Apr 2025. The two outlets name the associate differently.

entities.title: Bidya Bhattarai resigns as education minister

properties.description: Education Minister Bidya Bhattarai resigned amid differences with the prime minister and finance minister; a health reason was also stated.

document_url.label: Education minister resigns after rift with PM, finance minister

evidence.note: Date derived from 'on Monday' in a 22 Apr article. Reasons conflict.

entities.title: Supreme Court upholds Lamichhane's custody

properties.description: The Supreme Court upheld Rabi Lamichhane's custody in the cooperative fraud case, saying it could not reasonably be believed on the available evidence that the defendants were innocent.

document_url.label: Supreme Court upholds custody of Rabi Lamichhane in cooperative fraud case

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post, 23 May 2025.

entities.title: Communications ministry notice: social media platforms must register within seven days

properties.description: The Ministry of Communication and Information Technology required unregistered social media platforms to register by 4 September 2025, in line with the Supreme Court directive, designating a point of contact, a resident grievance handling officer and a compliance officer.

document_url.label: Radio Nepal Online report on the social media registration notice

evidence.note: Radio Nepal Online, 28 Aug 2025. This belongs to the 28 Aug to 7 Sep phase and may also be recorded by the ban-and-mobilisation topic.

entities.title: 2024 floods: at least 224 dead

properties.statement: At the 1 Oct 2024 count the September 2024 floods and landslides had killed 224 people and injured 158, with 24 missing.
properties.verification_note: Competing tolls for the same event: 217 (URL of the AP story), 219 (Global Voices), 224 (AP text), 249 (Nepal Economic Forum, 2025). Counting date and categories are not stated.

evidence.note: The two copies are one AP story.

entities.title: 2024 floods: at least 219 dead

properties.statement: The September 2024 floods and landslides killed at least 219 people and displaced over 12,000 families.
properties.verification_note: See the 224 and 249 claims.

evidence.note: Global Voices, 2 Oct 2024; the retrieved text paraphrased this figure.

entities.title: 2024 floods: 249 dead

properties.statement: The flooding led to 249 deaths, 177 injuries and the displacement of more than 10,000 families.
properties.verification_note: A later total than the AP and Global Voices figures; the source does not say what it counts.

evidence.note: Nepal Economic Forum, 5 May 2025.

entities.title: Oli government's flood response was slow and under-prepared

entities.title: Tinkune violence: hundreds injured

properties.statement: The 28 March Tinkune violence left two dead and hundreds injured.

evidence.note: IANS paraphrase (no verbatim sentence retrieved).

entities.title: Tinkune turnout was 'hardly 5,000'

properties.statement: The 28 March pro-monarchy demonstration drew 'hardly 5,000' people.

entities.title: Supreme Court registration verdict dated 29 September 2024

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post, copied by Asia News Network.

entities.title: Supreme Court registration ruling dated 17 August 2025

properties.statement: The Supreme Court ruling that required registration of social media platforms was delivered on 17 August 2025.

evidence.note: CPJ, 4 Sep 2025.

entities.title: Social Media Bill introduced on Monday 27 January 2025

properties.statement: The government introduced the Social Media Bill in the National Assembly on Monday, reported on 29 to 30 January (27 Jan, derived).

evidence.note: Himalayan Times.

entities.title: Social Media Bill tabled on 29 January 2025

evidence.note: Nepal Economic Forum, 10 Feb 2025.

entities.title: Social Media Bill presented on 9 February 2025

properties.statement: The communications minister presented the social media bill in the National Assembly on 9 February 2025.

entities.title: The Social Media Bill threatens freedom of expression

entities.title: Education minister resigned for health reasons

entities.title: Education minister resigned over a rift on teachers' demands

properties.statement: Bidya Bhattarai resigned after the prime minister and the finance minister refused to fund teachers' salary and benefit demands, estimated at Rs150-200 billion a year.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post, 22 Apr 2025 (opening sentence quoted; cost estimate paraphrased).

entities.title: Lamichhane charges are politically motivated

properties.statement: Supporters of Rabi Lamichhane said the charges against him were politically motivated.

entities.title: Parliamentary committee concluded Lamichhane was involved in cooperative fund misuse
